subject.title: Memory/QMD: isolate mcporter sidecars per agent

question: Should OpenClaw own generated per-agent MCPorter configuration only for bare QMD stdio definitions while treating customized MCPorter definitions as externally owned?
rationale: That choice determines configuration authority, daemon identity, credential handling, and upgrade behavior for existing QMD users; source correctness alone cannot establish the intended permanent product boundary.

options.title: Approve the ownership split
options.body: Use generated per-agent configuration only for bare QMD stdio definitions and preserve every customized definition at its original MCPorter source.

options.title: Narrow to environment isolation
options.body: Land only separate QMD and MCPorter spawn environments and defer generated sidecar ownership to a smaller follow-up.

options.title: Pause the architecture
options.body: Keep current behavior until maintainers define another canonical QMD/MCPorter ownership model.

recommendation.title: Approve the ownership split
recommendation.body: Use generated per-agent configuration only for bare QMD stdio definitions and preserve every customized definition at its original MCPorter source.

likelyOwner.reason: The available history most directly connects this person to the existing per-agent MCPorter daemon-state behavior being expanded.
